newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end down on poor annual results.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end down on poor annual results.

text.p: China B shares ended down on Tuesday, pulled down by a series of poor company results in the last days of the corporate reporting season, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index fell 1.314 points or 1.45 percent to 89.356 on turnover of $19.544 million.
Eight B share companies posted 1996 results on Tuesday, most reporting falling profits.
Selling in companies with poor results dragged down the index, but the downward potential would be limited with strong support seen at 87 to 88 points, brokers said.
"The negative mood engendered by poor company results will be digested soon," said one broker. "The national economy has recovered, which will benefit listed firms in the long run."
Shanghai Shangling Electric Appliances was the worst performer on its poor results, plunging $0.038 or 9.89 percent to $0.346 on volume of 108,000 shares.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on profit-taking, down $0.022 or 1.49 percent to $1.450 on volume of 3.3 million shares.
The Shenzhen B index shed 0.64 points or 0.36 percent to 175.89 on turnover of HK$148.3 million.
Selling of firms with weak earnings set the tone for Tuesday's trading, brokers said.
SEZ Real Estate fell to its 10 percent daily limit-down in early morning trading for the second straight session after announcing poor 1996 annual results over the weekend.
It recovered much of the loss by the close but was still the worst performer with a fall of HK$0.17 or 4.18 percent to HK$3.90. Volume reached 2.4 million shares.
The company posted a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996, based on international accounting standards.
Shenzhen North Jianshe Motorcycle was the top gainer despite announcing sharply lower profits for 1996. It closed at its 10 percent limit-up of HK$3.81 on volume of 827,100 shares.
"Although the results were terrible, they beat expectations as the motor industry had gone through a rough year," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
Jianshe said net profits for 1996 plunged to 50.73 million yuan from 288.71 million in 1995 based on international accounting standards.
Losses in the Shenzhen domestic currency A share market contributed to the B share dips, traders said.
The Shenzhen A share index lost 3.52 points or 0.72 percent to 484.72 on turnover of 14.9 billion yuan.

Shanghai's A share index rose 27.161 points or 1.92 percent to 1,439.086 points on volume of 748.3 million shares worth 9.9 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index gained 39.750 points or 1.02 percent to 3,944.245 points.
